topicName: MLlib and Distributed Machine Learning Workflows
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: MLlib and Distributed Machine Learning Workflows in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache Spark MLlib is Apache Spark's scalable machine learning library. Its goal is to make practical machine learning scalable and easy. At a high level, it provides tools such as machine learning algorithms, feature engineering utilities, pipelines, and persistence mechanisms for saving models."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Concepts of MLlib"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DataFrame-based API: MLlib's primary machine learning API is built on top of DataFrames. DataFrames provide a rich set of data types, schema definitions, and optimizations."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pipelines: MLlib uses the concept of Pipelines to unify ML workflows, making it easy to combine multiple algorithms into a single workflow or pipeline."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Transformers: Algorithms that can transform one DataFrame into another DataFrame, such as feature extractors and models."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Estimators: Algorithms that can fit on a DataFrame to produce a Transformer, such as a machine learning algorithm that trains on data."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up the Spark Session"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before building our distributed machine learning workflow, we must initialize a SparkSession, which is the entry point to programming Spark with the Dataset and DataFrame API."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("MLlibDistributedWorkflow") \
    .getOrCreate()"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Building a Machine Learning Pipeline"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us create a complete end-to-end pipeline that includes data loading, feature assembling, model training using Logistic Regression, and evaluation."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
from pyspark.ml.classification import LogisticRegression
from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler
from pyspark.sql import Row

# Sample distributed data generation
data = [
    Row(features=[0.1, 1.2, 0.3], label=0.0),
    Row(features=[0.5, 0.2, 0.9], label=1.0),
    Row(features=[0.2, 0.8, 0.4], label=0.0),
    Row(features=[0.9, 0.5, 0.1], label=1.0)
]

df = spark.createDataFrame(data)

# Define feature assembler
assembler = VectorAssembler(inputCols=["features"], outputCol="assembled_features")

# Initialize Logistic Regression
lr = LogisticRegression(featuresCol="assembled_features", labelCol="label")

# Construct the Pipeline
pipeline = Pipeline(stages=[assembler, lr])

# Train the model
model = pipeline.fit(df)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Evaluating and Saving the Model"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the model is trained across the distributed cluster, you can use it to make predictions on test data and persist the trained pipeline to disk for future inference runs."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Make predictions on the same or test dataset
predictions = model.transform(df)

# Select operational columns to display
predictions.select("features", "label", "probability", "prediction").show()

# Save the fitted pipeline model to disk
model.write().overwrite().save("/tmp/logistic_regression_pipeline")"}]
